title: No Coast, Two Seas: Sailing Balaton and Paddling the Tisza Flooded Forest
subRegion: Lake Balaton, Lake Tisza, the Szigetköz Danube branches and Lake Velence

bestPeriod.window: the first three weeks of June and the first two weeks of September — water still 21–24 °C, wind reliable, shores empty
bestPeriod.avoid: 20 July–20 August (the whole country is on the lake; Kékszalag week closes Balatonfüred's harbour to visiting boats)

transport.note: €140–€230 (hire car or MÁV rail passes plus the Szántód–Tihany ferry)

activities.note: €260–€480 (sailing charter or course, two windsurf/wing days, kayak and SUP hire)

hook: Hungary has no coastline and never has. What it has instead is a 77 km inland sea that behaves like open water in a squall, and a flooded forest on a dammed river that behaves like a maze. This week is four days of wind on Balaton — keelboat sailing out of Balatonfüred, wingfoiling off the Kenese bluffs — and three of quiet paddling through the willow labyrinth of Lake Tisza. No tides, no swell, and one genuinely serious hazard you must learn to read.

snapshot.Start / End: Balatonfüred → Tiszafüred (point-to-point, ~250 km between the two lakes)
snapshot.Getting there: Budapest Ferenc Liszt (BUD). MÁV line 29 from Déli/Kelenföld to Balatonfüred, ~2 h; line 30 to Siófok on the south shore. Lake Tisza is 2 h by car from Budapest on the M3; rail to Tiszafüred via Füzesabony.

itinerary.title: Balatonfüred, the sailing capital
itinerary.morning: Train from Budapest to **Balatonfüred**. Walk the Tagore sétány promenade and the Vitorlás tér harbour, and check in with your school or charter — paperwork and licence checks happen before anything gets untied.
itinerary.afternoon: A first sail on the eastern basin as the thermal fills after 13:00. Reaching towards Tihany, tacking back, learning what 3.3 m of water does to wave shape.
itinerary.evening: Fish soup on the promenade and the **Kékszalag** history: the Blue Ribbon, run since 1934, is Europe's longest round-the-lake race, roughly 155 km from Balatonfüred to Balatonkenese, Keszthely, Tihany and back, held in **mid-July** [VERIFY: 2026 Kékszalag dates].

itinerary.title: The Tihany narrows
itinerary.morning: Ashore on the **Tihany peninsula**: the Benedictine abbey, the Inner Lake, and the view down onto the narrows where the lake constricts to about 1.5 km.
itinerary.afternoon: Sail the narrows on the afternoon breeze — the strongest, gustiest water on Balaton, with the 12 m well underneath and noticeably colder water on your hands.
itinerary.evening: Ride the **Szántód–Tihany car ferry** across and back for the crossing itself, then eat at Zamárdi on the shallow south shore [VERIFY: current Szántódrév ferry season and timetable].

itinerary.title: Kenese and the wing day
itinerary.morning: Drive or take the train 25 km east to **Balatonkenese** under the Akarattya loess bluffs. Rig on the Vak Bottyán strand and wait; nothing happens before midday.
itinerary.afternoon: The northwesterly comes in side-on across a long fetch — the best windsurf and wingfoil water on the lake. Beginners should be at **Balatonalmádi** or the southern shore instead, where you can stand up.
itinerary.evening: Watch the **viharjelző** lamp on the shore mast as the light goes. Learn to count the flash rate now, in calm weather, so you are not doing it for the first time in a squall.

itinerary.title: The shallow south shore
itinerary.morning: Cross to **Siófok** or **Zamárdi**. The southern shore shelves so gently you can walk 300 m out in waist-deep water at 25 °C — this is where every Hungarian learns, and where a first windsurf or SUP lesson belongs.
itinerary.afternoon: A long SUP paddle along the Zamárdi shoreline, or a beginner windsurf session. Nothing here is deeper than you are tall, which is the whole point.
itinerary.evening: Drive east to **Tiszafüred**, about 3 h via the M7 and M3. Alternatively, spend the evening on **Lake Velence** at Agárd, halfway, and finish the transfer in the morning.

itinerary.title: Into the flooded forest
itinerary.morning: At **Poroszló**, start at the **Tisza-tavi Ökocentrum** — the freshwater aquarium and the marsh walkway give you the map of the labyrinth before you enter it.
itinerary.afternoon: Kayak from the Poroszló port into the **Tiszavalki basin**: dead-straight cut channels opening into willow and poplar standing in the water, storks, terns and herons overhead. Carry a compass or GPS track; the channels look identical.
itinerary.evening: Tiszafüred for *halászlé* — Tisza fish soup, river carp, far hotter with paprika than the Balaton version.

itinerary.title: Tiszafüred, birds and open water
itinerary.morning: The **Tiszafüredi madárrezervátum** bird reserve is part of Hortobágy National Park, and its core zone can only be entered **with a guide or a permit** — book a guided paddle rather than blundering into it [VERIFY: current Hortobágy NP guided-paddle booking and permit rules].
itinerary.afternoon: SUP on the open water of the **Sarud basin**, where the lake widens and behaves like a lake rather than a forest. Wind here is lighter and more variable than on Balaton.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the Tiszafüred embankment. Lake Tisza is a reservoir on a dammed river, so unlike Balaton it has a **slow but real current** near the main channel and at the Kisköre dam — stay clear of both.

itinerary.title: Szigetköz or the drive home
itinerary.morning: Either a last Tisza paddle, or the long option: drive northwest to the **Szigetköz**, the Danube's braided side-branch system above Győr, and put a canoe in at **Lipót** or **Ásványráró**.
itinerary.afternoon: The Szigetköz branches are gravel-bedded, cold, clear and genuinely flowing — the only moving water on this trip. Go with a local outfitter; the branches are shallow and shift annually.
itinerary.evening: Győr or Budapest for the flight home, three water bodies and three different rulebooks behind you.

accommodationStrategy.name: Harbour-side hotels and pensions
accommodationStrategy.description: walking distance to the yacht harbour, so you are on the boat when the thermal fills rather than driving to it. Board and rig storage is normal; ask when booking.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 6–10 weeks ahead for June, and avoid Kékszalag week unless you are racing [VERIFY: current Balatonfüred June rates].

accommodationStrategy.name: Beach-side apartments
accommodationStrategy.description: the eastern-basin wind ground, strand 200 m away, space for a board bag and a wing. Much cheaper than Füred and better water for foiling.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 4–6 weeks ahead; weekly lets are standard and cheaper than nightly.

accommodationStrategy.name: Port guesthouses
accommodationStrategy.description: paddle-in access, drying space, and a 06:00 launch onto flat water before the day-trippers. Both towns are quiet, cheap and built around the water.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 weeks ahead in July–August; a few days outside that.

logistics.connectivity: Full coverage on both lakes. Install the OMSZ weather app and bookmark the **viharjelző** status page; the warning is also broadcast on lakeside loudspeakers and shown at every harbour.
logistics.emergency: **112**, reaching the **Balatoni vízirendészet** and the Hungarian water-rescue service. Give the nearest named strand or harbour. Life jackets are compulsory on small craft; wear one on a SUP regardless of what the locals do.
logistics.weather: The defining risk. Cold fronts cross the Bakony fast, the lake builds steep chop within minutes, and the shallow depth means no swell warns you first. **Check the storm warning before every launch and again at 12:00.** Second degree means everyone off the water, swimmers included.
logistics.bookingWindows: Charters and courses 6–10 weeks for June, longer around the Kékszalag; guided Hortobágy paddles 2–3 weeks. Everything else is short-notice.
logistics.money: Hungary uses the **forint**, roughly 395–400 HUF to €1 [VERIFY: current HUF/EUR rate]. Cards work at harbours, schools and restaurants; beach kiosks and small rentals are often cash. Decline dynamic currency conversion at ATMs.
logistics.transportRules: MÁV serves both Balaton shores (lines 29 and 30) and Tiszafüred via Füzesabony; the **Szántód–Tihany ferry** links the shores in season. **Petrol and diesel motorboats are banned on Balaton.** Skipper alcohol limits follow the road **KRESZ** rules, and the water police test.
logistics.permits: No licence for boards, wings, kayaks or SUPs. **A Hungarian licence or recognised equivalent (typically an ICC) is required to skipper a keelboat** — confirm in writing with the charter company before paying. The Tiszafüred reserve core zone needs a guide or permit, and parts of Lake Tisza close in the breeding season.

proTips: **Learn the flash rate on a calm day.** Forty-five per minute means come in; ninety means get out now. Counting for ten seconds and doubling is the whole skill, and it is the one that matters.
**Sail Balaton mornings for practice, afternoons for fun.** The thermal is a clock. Schools run drills before noon because there is nothing else to do with the water.
**Send your ICC to the charter company before you pay the deposit.** Licence recognition is the most common reason a Balaton bareboat booking collapses at the desk.
**Beginners go south, foilers go east.** Zamárdi and Siófok for waist-deep warm water; Kenese and Almádi for the side-on northwesterly. Do not learn at Tihany.
**Take a GPS track into the Tiszavalki channels.** The flooded forest is genuinely a maze, the willow stands look identical, and phone batteries die.
**Go the first week of September.** The water is still 22–23 °C, the wind is back to its May reliability, and the strands that were impassable in August are empty.

**Eat the two fish soups in the right order.** Balaton *halászlé* is milder and pike-perch-based; the Tisza version is carp, darker and far hotter. Doing Balaton first makes the Tisza one land properly.

raw.Prevailing wind: The dominant direction is **northwesterly**, funnelled and accelerated by the Bakony hills. The reliable pattern is a **thermal building from about 13:00** and holding to early evening, usually 10–18 knots, strongest through the **Tihany narrows** where the lake pinches to about 1.5 km. Mornings are light — schools use them for drills. Most consistent wind in **May, June and September**; July and August are hotter, busier and often glassy until mid-afternoon.
raw.There are no tides: Balaton is a closed inland lake: **no tide, no swell, no current worth the name**. The hazards are different and entirely real. First, **squall lines** — a cold front crossing the Bakony arrives with almost no warning. Second, the **chop**: with a mean depth of about **3.3 m** (maximum roughly 12 m in the Tihany well), the lake cannot absorb energy, so wind that would raise a long swell at sea instead raises a **short, steep, vicious chop within minutes** that stops a dinghy dead and swamps a SUP. Third, **cold** — the deep basin off Tihany stays markedly colder than the shallows, and going from 26 °C at Zamárdi into the channel is a genuine shock. A slow wind-driven **seiche** shifts water end to end; that matters for moorings, not for you.
raw.The viharjelző — storm warning system: The most important thing on the lake, and not advisory. Orange-yellow lamps on masts around the whole shoreline flash at a rate that encodes the alert. **First degree: 45 flashes per minute** — storm possible; leave deep water and stay within roughly 500 m of shore. **Second degree: 90 flashes per minute** — storm imminent or in progress; **leave the water immediately**, no exceptions. Read the rate, not the colour: count for ten seconds and double it. Warnings come from the national meteorological service and are enforced by the water police [VERIFY: current viharjelző flash rates, lamp colours and issuing authority]. Never gamble on outrunning a second degree — the chop builds faster than you can reach a harbour.
raw.Launch spots by name: **Balatonfüred** — the Balatonfüredi Yacht Club harbour and the town marina, the keelboat centre of the lake. **Balatonkenese** and **Balatonalmádi** — the eastern basin under the Akarattya bluffs, side-on northwesterly, the windsurf and wingfoil ground. **Tihany** — the narrows, strongest and gustiest, experienced only. **Siófok** and **Zamárdi** — the shallow warm southern shore where you can wade 300 m out; beginner ground, and where every school teaches. **Lake Tisza** — the harbours at **Poroszló** and **Tiszafüred**. **Szigetköz** — canoe put-ins at **Dunakiliti**, **Lipót** and **Ásványráró**. **Lake Velence** — Agárd and Gárdony, shallow and reed-fringed.
raw.Rental and school hubs: Sailing schools and charter fleets cluster at Balatonfüred and Balatonlelle; windsurf and wing bases sit on the Balatonkenese (Vak Bottyán strand), Balatonalmádi (Wesselényi strand) and Zamárdi beaches. Kayak, canoe and SUP hire on Lake Tisza runs from the **Tisza-tavi Ökocentrum** port at Poroszló and the Tiszafüred harbours [VERIFY: current school and rental operator names and season dates at each site]. Reckon €50–€90 a day for windsurf or wing gear with a lesson, €12–€25 for a kayak or SUP, €200–€400 for a skippered keelboat [VERIFY: current 2026 charter and gear rates].
raw.Licences and boating rules: To **skipper a keelboat** on Hungarian waters you need a Hungarian small-craft licence (*kedvtelési célú kishajóvezetői*, with the sailing endorsement) **or a recognised equivalent — an ICC is the usual accepted foreign qualification**. This catches people out: charter firms will not release a yacht on a foreign club membership, and a bareboat booking made without checking is a booking you lose [VERIFY: current licence thresholds and which foreign certificates are recognised]. **Petrol and diesel motorboats are banned on Balaton** for recreational use — sail, paddle and electric only, with exemptions for authorities and rescue. Boards, wings, kayaks and SUPs need no licence. The **Balatoni vízirendészet** enforces the code, with life jackets required on small craft and alcohol limits matching the road **KRESZ** rules.
